text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — noticed tail-latency regressions on Dedicated pools when mixed-tenant offload thrash happens. Proposing we add a per-tenant soft-reserve + scheduled compaction window to avoid eviction storms. Anyone else seen this?
Chandra: Yep. Hit this on prod cluster-7 last Wed. Evictor floods host staging and we end up with long GPU stall spikes (~200-400ms).
Jess: Seen it too. TL;DR: eviction concurrency + fragmentation => repeated refills and KV-cache churn. Soft-reserve would keep a small working set pinned so small bursts don't trigger full-blown rehydrate.
Sam: What are main tradeoffs? CPU cost of compaction vs tail latency. Also how do we surface this without stabbing allocator ABI too much?
Kai: We can keep allocator API stable if we add a tenant-level reservation token that the scheduler honors. No allocator changes required, just enforcement at admission/evictor layer.
Chandra: Right. Two levers: (1) soft-reserve (quota of resident pages per tenant) and (2) delayed compaction window (post-evict cooldown). Soft-reserve reduces eviction frequency; compaction reduces fragmentation over time.
Jess: Sketch of config (pseudo):
```
tenant_policies:
  - tenant_id: T123
    soft_reserve_pages: 4096
    compaction_window_ms: 5000
    compaction_budget_pct: 10
```
Sam: compaction_budget_pct = percent of CPU budget to use for background compaction?
Jess: yeah. small steady budget so we don't spike CPU. Also run compaction only when tail latency < X and GPU queue depth < Y.
Kai: We'll need new telemetry: compaction_score, reclaim_rate, eviction_retries. Then use it to decide can_compact_now().
Chandra: Important: compaction can make fragmentation temporarily worse if done at wrong time (causes page migrations). We should prefer low-util windows and prefer host staging coalescing rather than GPU-side moves.
Sam: How about admission/backpressure hooks? If tenant uses > soft_reserve we throttle new request admission before evicting more pages. That prevents immediate refills.
Jess: Agreed. Admission throttle = token bucket tied to soft_reserve usage. Simple: if resident_pages > soft_reserve * 1.1 then reduce admission rate by 50%.
Kai: Implementation note: add a lightweight per-tenant state machine in the routing layer. States: NORMAL, SOFT_THROTTLE, COMPACTING, HARD_THROTTLE. Transitions based on metrics windows.
Chandra: Another corner — pinning latency-sensitive embeddings. We should allow an explicit "pin list" that bypasses soft-reserve eviction. Small list, user-specified (or eval-determined).
Sam: Good point. Need API surface: per-request flags or retention TTLs?
Jess: TTLs + explicit pin flag. TTLs default to short so we don't keep wasteful pins.
Kai: Ops question: how will Dedicated SLAs account for soft-reserve? Do we guarantee pinned working set?
Chandra: For Dedicated, we document a best-effort soft-reserve; true hard guarantees require reserved capacity bump. But we should surface expected tail-latency improvements in the console.
Sam: Actionable next steps:
- draft short RFC describing soft-reserve tokens, admission hooks, compaction window, telemetry (owner: Jess)
- prototype per-tenant state machine in routing (owner: Kai)
- add compaction runner + budget controls to evictor (owner: Chandra)
- perf harness on cluster-7 to simulate mixed-tenant thrash (owner: Sam)
Jess: I'll start the RFC and include config examples + eval matrix.
Kai: I'll stub the state machine and a simple admission throttle.
Chandra: I'll prototype compaction budget and low-util detection.
ops-bot: Created issue #4821: "soft-reserve + compaction for Dedicated pools" and assigned to Jess, Kai, Chandra.
Sam: Nice, thanks. Any objections to target an RFC by EOW?
Jess: EOW ok for draft. Will ping for review.
Kai: Sounds good. I'll add a tiny perf test to CI so we can measure regressions.
Chandra: One more note — include a flag to disable compaction under on-prem/private deployments for CPU-constrained customers.
Sam: Good catch. Document caveats.
Jess: (reacted with :thumbsup:)
Kai: (reacted with :eyes:)
Sam: OK moving this to RFC channel after draft. Thanks all.
